title: Ethiopian Chicken Gored Gored Style
community: Ethiopia — chicken prepared in the raw-and-spiced tradition
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Doro Gored — chicken breast cut into cubes, very quickly sautéed in mitmita-infused kibbeh, remaining slightly pink inside. The chicken version of Gored Gored — briefer cooking, more chilli heat, served with injera as a spicy starter.
longDesc: Doro Gored applies the gored gored philosophy to chicken — the cubes are seared very briefly in intensely spiced kibbeh until just cooked but still very moist at the centre. This requires very high heat and very fresh chicken.
steps: Warm kibbeh. Add mitmita. Infuse 1 minute. Remove from heat.
Heat clean pan until smoking hot.
Add infused kibbeh. Add chicken cubes in a single layer.
Sear 2 minutes per side — just cooked through to 74°C.
Add garlic, awaze, and salt. Toss.
chefTips: Internal temperature of 74°C is mandatory — unlike beef gored gored, chicken cannot be served raw.
The cooking is still fast — the goal is seared outside, just-set inside.
cookingScience: Unlike beef gored gored, chicken gored gored is always cooked to 74°C — the Salmonella and Campylobacter risk of undercooked chicken is significantly higher than beef. However, cooking to exactly 74°C rather than higher preserves the maximum moisture and juiciness.
sustainabilityTips: Chicken breast — the leanest possible protein.
culturalNote: Doro Gored brings the gored gored spirit to chicken — the same intensity of spice and immediacy of service, the same emphasis on the freshest possible ingredient, but with the food safety adjustment that chicken demands.
